newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government to present decree on milk dispute.
newsitem.headline: Italian government to present decree on milk dispute.

text.p: The Italian government said on Monday it would present a decree law soon to try to resolve a dispute by dairy farmers over EU fines for milk overproduction.
A statement from Prime Minister Romano Prodi's office said the package of incentives had been given the green light by the European Commission.

The package, to be discussed at the next cabinet meeting, would include low-interest loans, grants to make up for lost income, and a restructuring of milk production. A commission of inquiry will be set up to review the dairy sector.
Farmers organisations welcomed the initiative as an initial step to resolving the dispute.

The government statement said milk producers had asked to be allowed to pay eventual fines in instalments before the Italian commission completes its work. The European Commission has not yet commented on this proposal, the statement said.
Producers' organisations said the government had proposed that farmers pay a first instalment of 25 percent of the fines but they hoped for a lower initial payment.
The government said it would sponsor parliamentary reforms of dairy production, including a modification of quotas.
Agriculture Minister Michele Pinto has asked the European Commission to raise Italy's quota to 10.5 million tonnes.
The cabinet is next expected to meet on Thursday.
The statement was issued after meetings between government representatives, headed by Prodi and Pinto, and farmer's representatives.

The dispute, which has been accompanied by nearly two weeks of road blocks, centres on European Union "super-levy" fines, due to be paid by Friday, for overshooting Italy's national 1995-96 milk quota of 9.9 million tonnes by some 400,000 tonnes.
The fines add up to some 370 billion lire ($230 million).
Farmers, who say the government is to blame for miscalculating the quotas thus allowing them to overproduce, have welcomed the idea of a commission.
Farmers say that the fines would be ruinous and have taken to the roads in their tractors to draw attention to their plight, blocking airports and highways.
National airline Alitalia said it would sue the dairy farmers for damages to cover the billions of lire it said it had lost because of flight delays and cancellations.
Farmers dismantled blockades in the financial capital Milan ahead of the talks with Prodi but staged protests near Turin, at Verona and Venice airports and on a main southern motorway.
Under the quota system, national farmers produce just over half of the 18 million tonnes of milk Italy consumes.
